instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on.
Slice the pork thinly across the grain. Transfer it to a bowl and add the wine, the cornstarch, 1 tsp of the soy sauce and half the ginger, grated. Mix and leave it while you prep.

Cut the cabbage into bite-size pieces. That should be about 8 cups. Cut the other half of the ginger into thin matchsticks, slice the garlic and cut the scallions into 1 inch pieces, keeping the whites and greens apart.
In a small bowl, stir the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, the sugar, the salt and the sesame oil.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it's smoking. Add 1 tbsp of the oil and spread the pork in a single layer. Leave it for 1 minute, until it's browned underneath. Stir for 1 minute and transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining 2 tbsp oil. Add the garlic, ginger and scallion whites and stir for 15 seconds.
Add the cabbage. Leave it for 1 minute, then stir, and repeat for 4 minutes in all, until the edges are browned and the cabbage is just tender.

Return the pork and any juices to the wok, pour in the sauce and add the scallion greens. Toss for 1 minute. You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it should have no raw pink.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version found had 20 or more ratings, so this leads with the best-rated one I could read. The versions agree on thin sliced pork seared first, then cabbage in the same pan with garlic and ginger; one uses pork belly and plain seasoning, the other tenderloin with a soy sauce and cornstarch slurry. This version uses tenderloin and skips the slurry so the cabbage stays dry and browned. Total is 22 minutes.
